## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Katāpattivāra* ("The number of offenses within each rule", Pvr 2.2) is a specialized analytical chapter in the *Parivāra*, the closing book of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Functioning as an exegetical catechism, the chapter systematically defines the number of sub-offences or secondary infractions that may be incurred upon breaking each rule of the monastic code [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the text has been made available by Bhikkhu Brahmali on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].
While SuttaCentral does not catalog curated cross-canonical parallels for this section [SuttaCentral], automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus reveals widespread internal textual reuse, identifying 4,490 matching passages across 154 other Pali works [DharmaNexus]. Its most extensive textual relationships exist within the *Parivāra* itself, predominantly with the earlier *Katāpattivāra* (Pvr 1.2), as well as Pvr 1.10, the *Katthapaññattivāra* (Pvr 2.1 and Pvr 2.10), and the *Antarapeyyāla* (Pvr 4) [DharmaNexus]. It also exhibits significant phraseological overlap with the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha*, individual rule analyses in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* (such as Pārājika 2) and *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (such as Pācittiya 67 and 73), and post-canonical or commentarial compendia like the *Vinayavinicchaya*, the *Parivāra-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Vajirabuddhi-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus aligns passages in the *Katāpattivāra* with corresponding rule formulations in external Vinaya traditions, including the Sanskrit *Prātimokṣasūtra*, *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya*, *Poṣadhavastu*, and *Pravāraṇāvastu*, alongside Tibetan translations of the *Vinayasūtra* (D4117), *Bhikṣuṇīprātimokṣasūtra* (D0004), *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-4), and *Vinaya-uttaragrantha* (D0007) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
